items.title: Frank Goudie Interview
items.q: We became close friends together ever since.

ctx.x: Yeah. The memory of those guys sort of went, was going through you when you were picking up the instrument,

right? I couldn't forget it. I couldn't forget it. Yeah. I couldn't forget it. Impossible. Because those guys, they, they played it at nobody else. They, they're the creators of, of, of, of jazz, and, and you can't get around it. There's nobody ever played like they played then and what they are playing today. Nobody may ever again. No. Well, the future we can't tell, but for sure nobody have done it. Yeah. Yeah. Now you take Sidney Baxter, if you picture what he played at that time and what Sidney was playing…

Well, the, the horn practically blew up in his hands, so. Great man. Uh, you were telling me when you were over there, let's see, this would be, uh, oh, a long time later, uh, that, uh, I always got the impression when I hear him that, my God, he frightened you to death to be in the same room with him. Is that so? To you?
